_doc: NOTICES — the screen's traffic controller (D-153, D-154). One system decides WHERE and WHEN transient text is allowed to exist, so five owners can no longer shout over each other. Five fixed regions: TOP-CENTRE is the police WANTED/EVADED band (reserved here, drawn by police.gd); TOP-RIGHT under the cash readout is the TICKER (money, respect, promotions — one short line each, newest on top, three at most); CENTRE-UPPER-THIRD is the CARD (one at a time, gated on the player being stopped, capped in size, clipped so type can never spill past its own panel); BOTTOM-RIGHT is mission_kit's LONGHORN app panel; BOTTOM-CENTRE is hud_gta's objective line. Read once at boot by scripts/systems/notices.gd. All values are in the 1600x900 logical UI space (project.godot stretch mode is canvas_items, so a 1280x720 window is this same layout x0.8).
_tuning: band_bottom 158, NOT the 130 the brief assumed: police.gd:588 pins WANTED at PRESET_CENTER_TOP margin 70 with a 46 px font (70..134) and police.gd:596 pins the reason subline at margin 126 with a 22 px font (126..157). A band that stopped at 130 would let a card's title land on top of the reason for the star. ticker_top 168 clears hud_gta's top-right stack: MARGIN 18 + star row (30 px font) + weapon (19) + ammo (26) + cash (24) with separation 2 measures ~154 in the shipped plate ($1,050 sits at 1600-space y 117..143). card_centre_y 0.30 puts the card's middle at y 270 of 900 — high enough that the road surface from y 390 down, where a target vehicle is (507..720 in order_debtor.png), is never covered, and low enough that it is not mistaken for the police band. card_w 900 is 56% of the frame (the old veil was 112%); card_h 220 is enforced by clip_contents, so type can never spill past the panel again. card_wait_max 4.0 / card_speed_gate 2.0: a card is a thing you READ, so it waits for you to stop; four seconds is the longest a payout should stay unacknowledged, and 2 m/s is a walking pace — below it nothing on screen is moving fast enough to matter. ticker_seconds 2.4 x 3 rows means the ticker can absorb a payout, a respect tick and a promotion inside one delivery without any of them reaching the middle of the screen. ticket_w 320: a card that is interrupted by a live objective does not vanish (the player earned it) — it becomes a receipt in the corner for the rest of its six seconds. card_w_narrow 560 / card_h_min 120: the card fits its content instead of filling a fixed slab — four rows or fewer stay in one column at 560 px wide, and the height is the box's own combined minimum clamped into 120..220, so a three-row RECOVERED receipt is a receipt and a seven-row COMIN' DOWN contract is a contract. The 220 cap is enforced twice: by the clamp, and by clip_contents on the panel — which is the actual D-153 fix, since the old card's 290 px of type SPILLED out of its own 190 px veil and that spill is what the plate shows.
